titre: The Lemming Suicide Was Filmed in Alberta
accroche: The scene of lemmings hurling themselves into the sea comes from a 1958 Disney film. It was shot far from the Arctic, with animals pushed off a cliff.
contenu_vulgarise:
Many small rodents run toward a cliff, hardly hesitate, then plunge into the waves. The scene has stuck in people's memories: it makes the lemming the emblem of blind obedience, and the expression “to behave like lemmings” has entered everyday language. It comes from a film, and that film manufactured it.

White Wilderness, released on August 12, 1958, belongs to Disney's “True-Life Adventures” series, award-winning wildlife documentaries. This one won the Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature at the 1959 ceremony. Its lemming segment shows a migration that ends in collective drowning, narrated as a mysterious urge of the species.

## What the Shoot Really Was

The place first: Alberta, a landlocked Canadian province, outside the lemmings' natural range. The “sea” in the film was a river. According to the Alaska Department of Fish and Game, the filmmakers had bought the animals from Inuit children in Manitoba, two provinces away. According to the investigation aired in 1982 by the Canadian program The Fifth Estate (CBC), in the report titled Cruel Camera, the same small group of lemmings was transported to the site, spun on turntables, then pushed repeatedly off a cliff. The Alaska Department of Fish and Game and the site Hyperallergic specify that these turntables were covered with snow. Hyperallergic adds that a cameraman on the crew, Bill Carrick, claimed that Manitoba children had been paid twenty-five cents to capture lemmings. The editing did the rest: a few individuals, filmed in tight shots, give the illusion of a crowd.

These details come from secondhand accounts, whose versions differ on secondary points. The core does not vary: the scene was staged, and the zoologist Gordon Jarrell answers unequivocally that lemmings do not commit suicide.

## What Lemmings Really Do

Their numbers fluctuate strongly from one year to the next, depending on predators, food, and climate. When they have exhausted the local food, the animals disperse. In the Scandinavian mountains, Jarrell reports, they can pile up at the water's edge, so numerous that they end up swimming across; soaked to the skin, they are in practice doomed. A description made at Barrow, Alaska, mentions drowned lemmings piled up on the shore. A dispersal that goes wrong is not a suicide: no death drive presides over it, only a risky crossing to escape hunger.

## The Shift

The story matters less for the lemming than for what it says about evidence: a convincing image, signed by a trusted brand and rewarded by the profession, fixed for decades an explanation that no observation supported. One wonders how many other scenes of nature, seen in childhood, were shot in another province.

repere.texte: The lemming segment of White Wilderness (1958) was shot in Alberta, a landlocked province outside the lemmings' range; the “sea” they plunge into was a river.
repere.source: Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Alaska Fish & Wildlife News, September 2003

carte.punch: Lemmings do not commit suicide. The film crew threw them off a cliff.
carte.idee: The iconic scene from White Wilderness (1958) was shot in Alberta, far from the Arctic, with a few lemmings spun on a turntable then thrown into the water. The species' real dispersal is a flight from hunger, not a death drive.

pour_aller_plus_loin.titre: CBC, The Fifth Estate — Cruel Camera (1982)

quiz.question: Why do lemmings sometimes die by drowning in the wild, according to the biologists cited?
choix: They disperse when food runs short, swim to cross, and some drown
They obey a regulating instinct that eliminates surplus individuals
They are drawn to the sea as a source of essential salt
They are pushed by the adults to reduce competition among the young
quiz.explication: Dispersal is a flight from hunger, with swimming as the means of crossing, hence the drownings. The sources cited invoke neither voluntary regulation, nor a quest for salt, nor pushing by the adults; the zoologist Gordon Jarrell says unequivocally that lemmings do not commit suicide.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Where was the lemming segment of White Wilderness shot?
choix: In the Arctic tundra of Svalbard
In Alberta, a landlocked province, outside the lemmings' range
On the Norwegian coast, during a real migration
In a Burbank studio, in front of a painted backdrop
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The shoot took place in Alberta, far from the species' natural range and far from any sea: the “sea” was a river.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What technique was used to simulate a migrating horde?
choix: Hundreds of lemmings released from a truck
A small number of animals spun on snow-covered turntables, filmed in tight shots
An optical effect made in a lab
quiz_supplementaire.explication: According to the ADFG and Hyperallergic, only a few dozen animals were spun on snow-covered turntables, and the editing produced the crowd effect.
